summary: Defines a YANG data model for configuring a Layer 2 provider-provisioned VPN service. A management system takes it as input and creates device-specific configuration for the network elements.

eli5.summary: This is an order form a customer fills out for a private link between sites. The provider's system turns it into the right settings.

questions: yang data model for layer 2 vpn
what is the l2vpn service model
what is the difference between vpws and vpls
subtitle: A YANG order form that lets a customer describe a Layer 2 VPN service, which the provider's management system then turns into device configuration.

tldr.problem: Providers sell Layer 2 VPN services (point-to-point and multipoint Ethernet connectivity between customer sites), but there was no common, machine-readable way for a customer to request one or for tools to exchange such a request.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8466 defines a YANG data model, ietf-l2vpn-svc, with two main containers: vpn-services for the VPN itself and sites for how each customer site attaches. A management system takes this request and generates the device-specific configuration.
tldr.outcome: It gives customers and operators a shared vocabulary for VPWS, VPLS and EVPN services over NETCONF or RESTCONF. It is a service model, not a device model, so it never configures network elements directly.

today: RFC 8466 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2018, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the specification of the L2VPN service model, a companion to the Layer 3 model in RFC 8299.

sections.title: What the L2VPN Service Model Is
sections.content:
RFC 8466 defines a YANG data model for a Layer 2 VPN (L2VPN) service, called the L2VPN Service Model (L2SM). Its elements can be used in communication protocols between customers and network operators, and as input to automated control and configuration applications.

The model covers point-to-point Virtual Private Wire Services (VPWS) and multipoint Virtual Private LAN Services (VPLS) that use pseudowires signaled with the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) and the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), as described in RFC 4761 and RFC 6624. It also covers Ethernet VPNs (EVPN) from RFC 7432, and it conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture in RFC 8342.

How a management system configures the network elements from this input is explicitly out of scope. The RFC also lists the L2VPN service types it builds on: LDP- or L2TP-signaled VPWS and VPLS, BGP-signaled VPLS, IP-only LAN services, BGP MPLS-based EVPN and EVPN VPWS.
sections.eli5: It is a standard order form for private links between offices. The form says what the customer wants, not how the provider's machines should be set up.

sections.title: Where the Model Sits in the Management Stack
sections.content:
The L2SM is an abstracted interface that a customer, who buys connectivity from a service provider (SP), uses to request, configure and manage the components of an L2VPN service. A typical use is as input to an orchestration layer that translates it into configuration commands for the network elements. Those commands may go out through a command line interface or through NETCONF with device-specific YANG models.

The reference architecture has a customer service requester talking L2SM to a service orchestration function, which works with a network orchestration function and a business and operations support application. The RFC says the model can be used by any component of the management system but not directly by network elements.

The RFC points to the Layer 3 VPN service model in RFC 8299 as a sibling to compare against, and to RFC 8309 and RFC 8199 for how service models relate to configuration models. It also contrasts itself with the Metro Ethernet Forum work, which covers the whole service lifecycle including billing and SLAs, whereas IETF service models are typically smaller and self-contained.
sections.eli5: The customer fills in the order form and the provider's back office turns it into settings for each machine. Nobody types the form straight into a router.

sections.title: The Shape of the Data Model
sections.content:
The module is named ietf-l2vpn-svc and is built so a provider can list multiple circuits of various service types for the same customer. A circuit is an end-to-end connection between two or more customer locations. The module has two main containers, vpn-services and sites, plus a vpn-profiles container that holds the identifiers the provider accepts (for example cloud and QoS profile identifiers).

Inside vpn-services, each vpn-service carries global parameters for one VPN: its vpn-id, a service type, the customer name, a topology, cloud access, frame delivery, extranet links and the ce-vlan-preservation and ce-vlan-cos-preservation settings.

A site holds at least one network access, and several in the case of multihoming. Attachment is through a bearer, meaning the properties below Layer 2, with a Layer 2 connection on top. Which sites may exchange traffic is expressed by the VPN policy or topology. The model is modular through YANG features (such as extranet VPNs, site diversity and QoS) and can be extended by augmentation, for example to add encapsulations beyond VXLAN.
sections.eli5: The form has two parts. One part describes the private network itself, and the other describes each office and how it plugs in.

sections.title: VPN Service Types and Topologies
sections.content:
The vpn-svc-type parameter supports six flavors: point-to-point VPWS between two sites, point-to-point or point-to-multipoint VPWS between a set of sites, multipoint VPLS between a set of sites, multipoint VPLS with root and leaf sites that blocks leaf-to-leaf traffic, EVPN, and EVPN VPWS. Other types can be added by augmentation.

For topology the module supports any-to-any (the default), Hub-and-Spoke (Hubs can exchange traffic) and Hub-and-Spoke Disjoint (Hubs cannot). In every hub topology, Spoke sites can talk only to Hub sites. In BGP-based VPNs the management system is expected to allocate Route Targets automatically, and to configure a MAC-VRF on the right provider edge devices. Each site then has a role in the topology: all sites in an any-to-any VPN MUST have the role any-to-any-role, while sites in hub topologies MUST be Hub or Spoke.

Two related features are shortcuts. The cloud-access container controls which sites may reach a public cloud or the Internet, using permit-site or deny-site lists, and by default all sites SHOULD be permitted. The extranet-vpns container lets one VPN reach all of another. The RFC warns that if VPN A lists VPN B as an extranet, all sites in VPN B also gain access to all sites in VPN A.
sections.eli5: You choose who may talk to whom. Everyone can chat with everyone, or the small offices can talk only to the head office, like spokes on a wheel.

sections.title: Sites and Site Network Accesses
sections.content:
A site represents a customer office connected to one or more VPN services, and it may have several locations. The model deals only with exterior interfaces (UNIs and NNIs); internal interfaces and the underlying topology are out of scope. A site has a site-id, devices, a management mode, locations, optional site diversity and a list of site-network-accesses.

Each site-network-access is an Ethernet logical connection to the site, and several of them are used for multihoming. The bearer says what the attachment needs below Layer 2, and the connection container sets Layer 2 parameters. The connection can be an untagged interface, a tagged interface or a LAG interface. For tagged interfaces the model defines five ways of tagging.

It also covers CVLAN-to-service mapping, preservation of the customer VLAN ID and CoS, Layer 2 control protocol handling (each protocol can be discarded, peered or tunneled), and Ethernet service OAM using IEEE 802.1ag connectivity fault management and ITU-T Y.1731 performance monitoring. Site management comes in three common models: provider-managed, customer-managed and co-managed CE.
sections.eli5: Each office can plug in with one cable or several. The form also says how the traffic is labeled and who looks after the office's router.

sections.title: Attaching Sites and Choosing Where to Connect
sections.content:
A site can be part of one or more VPNs, set by its site-vpn-flavor: single, multi, nni or e2e. Attachment happens at the site-network-access level in a mandatory vpn-attachment container, in one of two ways: reference the VPN directly by vpn-id together with a site-role, or reference a vpn-policy for more complex cases, such as a site that plays a Hub role in one VPN and an any-to-any role in another.

The management system then decides where each access connects (for example to a PE or an aggregation switch). It MUST honor all customer constraints, and if a constraint is too strict it MUST NOT provision the site and MUST tell the user which constraints failed. Placement can use the device the customer ordered, the site location, the access type (requested-type, strict, always-on, bearer-reference) and access diversity groups.

On the PE, the management system allocates a MAC-VRF and a Route Distinguisher that MUST be unique across all MAC-VRFs on that PE, or reuses an existing MAC-VRF that already fits. For availability, access-priority (higher is preferred) models primary/backup or load sharing, and redundancy-mode models single-active and active/active multihoming. The RFC gives a five-access example with priorities 100, 100, 50, 50 and 10, and notes some scenarios cannot be expressed this way.
sections.eli5: An office can join one private network or several. The provider has to follow the customer's wishes about where to plug in, or say clearly which wishes it could not meet.

sections.title: Bandwidth, QoS, Frame Delivery and MAC Limits
sections.content:
The service bandwidth is configured per site network access, using the Committed Information Rate, Excess Information Rate or Peak Information Rate, with separate ingress and egress values. The parameter has four types: bw-per-access, bw-per-cos, bw-per-svc and opaque bandwidth. The svc-mtu leaf can override the MTU derived from the physical interface.

QoS is an abstraction in two parts. A qos-classification-policy is an ordered list of rules that match traffic and set a target class, and frames are marked green, yellow or red depending on whether they fit the committed rate, only the excess rate, or neither. A qos-profile chooses a standard or custom scheduling profile with direction, policing, delay, jitter and a guaranteed bandwidth percentage. By default bandwidth is guaranteed only at the access, and an end-to-end leaf requests reservation across the transport network, though how is out of scope.

For broadcast, unknown unicast and multicast (BUM) traffic, the model supports bidirectional, shared and source-based trees and two ways to map multicast groups to ports. Providers can rate-limit BUM frames at the edge. To protect shared resources, mac-loop-prevention imposes a MAC move threshold, and mac-addr-limit caps learned MAC addresses and sets the action when the limit is hit: drop the packet, flood it, or log a warning.
sections.eli5: The form lets the customer say how fast the link should be and which traffic goes first. It also stops one noisy office from using up everybody's space in the shared address book.

sections.title: Carriers' Carriers, NNIs and Inter-Provider Use
sections.content:
For Carriers' Carriers (CsC), where a customer such as an ISP builds an MPLS service over a provider's L2VPN, the VPN service sets carrierscarrier to true and the site link runs LDP or BGP as the MPLS signaling protocol. With LDP an IGP MUST also be active, and with BGP signaling BGP MUST also be the routing protocol. The requested svc-mtu then refers to the MPLS MTU.

VPNs that span autonomous systems or providers need Network-to-Network Interfaces (NNIs), modeled as a site with site-vpn-flavor-nni. In option A, a back-to-back VPLS model, a VPN connection per VPN crosses the boundary on ASBR links and can be seen as a site. In option B, VPN routes are exchanged with MP-BGP, and the RFC distinguishes cases where no modeling is needed from cases where RT-filtering policy must be maintained. Option C is modeled like option B, but the MP-BGP session is multihop between routing gateway (RGW) nodes.

For end-to-end service across domains, the RFC describes stitching connectivity segments from site to site, so that control connections run only between PEs and ASBRs and not as a full mesh. The service orchestrator is assumed to see the complete abstract topology and resource availability.
sections.eli5: When a private network has to cross from one phone company to another, the two companies need an agreed handshake. The form has a way to order that handshake.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF. NETCONF's mandatory-to-implement secure transport is SSH (RFC 6242), and RESTCONF's is TLS (RFC 8446). The NETCONF access control model in RFC 8341 can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

The writable subtrees /l2vpn-svc/vpn-services/vpn-service and /l2vpn-svc/sites/site are sensitive because they indirectly create or modify PE and CE configuration, so unexpected changes could lead to service disruptions or network misbehavior. The same two subtrees are sensitive to read because they hold customer-confidential information such as customer name, site location and subscribed services.

When an SP serves multiple customers, it has to ensure each customer can view and modify only its own service information. The IANA section registers the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-l2vpn-svc and the YANG module name ietf-l2vpn-svc.
sections.eli5: The order forms hold secrets about customers and can change real networks. So only the right people may read or change them, and each customer sees only its own form.

viz.caption: FIVE VLAN TAGGING METHODS FOR A TAGGED INTERFACE

items.label: Priority tagged
items.desc: Packets are tagged with the frame priority level between CE and PE.

items.label: 802.1Q VLAN tagged
items.desc: Packets carry one or a set of customer VLAN (CVLAN) IDs.

items.label: Q-in-Q
items.desc: Multiple CVLAN IDs plus a single SP VLAN (SVLAN) tag.

items.label: Q-in-any
items.desc: Unknown CVLANs plus a single SVLAN tag.

items.label: VXLAN
items.desc: A VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI) and a peer list.

items.title: Provider-managed CE
items.text: The provider owns the CE and only the provider can access it. The boundary is between the CE and the customer network.

items.title: Customer-managed CE
items.text: The customer owns the CE and only the customer can access it. The boundary is between the PE and the CE.

items.title: Co-managed CE
items.text: The provider owns and manages the CE but gives the customer some configuration and monitoring access. The boundary is as for provider-managed.

items.label: Per access
items.desc: Rate enforcement for all service frames on a particular network access.

items.label: Per CoS
items.desc: Rate enforcement for all frames of a given CoS, which needs a cos-id.

items.label: Per service
items.desc: Rate enforcement for all frames of a particular VPN service, which needs a vpn-id.

items.label: Opaque
items.desc: Total bandwidth not tied to any cos-id, VPN service or site network access ID.
